LORD@Gen.1.1-Rev.description: Throughout the Bible, God is referred to by various names and titles, each revealing different aspects of His character, nature, and relationship with His people.
LORD@Gen.1.1-Rev.name: LORD

Laadah@1Ch.4.21.description: Laadah, a son of Shelah and descendant of Judah.
Laadah@1Ch.4.21.name: Laadah

Laban@Deu.1.1.description: Laban, a place where Moses spoke to the Israelites (<ref="Deu.1.1">Deu.1.1</ref>).
Laban@Deu.1.1.name: Laban

Laban@Gen.24.29-.description: Laban, the brother of Rebekah and father of Jacob's wives, Leah and Rachel.
Laban@Gen.24.29-.name: Laban

Lachish@Jos.10.3-Mic.description: Lachish, a fortified city in Judah, captured by Joshua and later by the Assyrians (<ref="Joshua 10; 2Ki.18.14, 19:8">Joshua 10; 2Ki.18.14, 19:8</ref>).
Lachish@Jos.10.3-Mic.name: Lachish

Lael@Num.3.24.description: Lael, the father of Eliasaph, a leader of the Gershonite Levites.
Lael@Num.3.24.name: Lael

Lahad@1Ch.4.2.description: Lahad, a descendant of Judah through Jahath.
Lahad@1Ch.4.2.name: Lahad

Lahmam@Jos.15.40.description: Lahmam, a city in the lowlands of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:40">Joshua 15:40</ref>).
Lahmam@Jos.15.40.name: Lahmam

Lahmi@2Sa.21.16-1Ch.description: Lahmi, the brother of Goliath, was killed by Elhanan the Bethlehemite.
Lahmi@2Sa.21.16-1Ch.name: Lahmi

Laish@1Sa.25.44-2Sa.description: Laish, the father of Palti (or 'Paltiel'), to whom Saul gave his daughter Michal in marriage.
Laish@1Sa.25.44-2Sa.name: Laish

Laishah@Isa.10.30.description: Laishah, a place near Anathoth and Gallim, mentioned in a prophecy of Isaiah (<ref="Isaiah 10:30">Isaiah 10:30</ref>).
Laishah@Isa.10.30.name: Laishah

Lakkum@Jos.19.33.description: Lakkum, a border town of the tribe of Naphtali (<ref="Joshua 19:33">Joshua 19:33</ref>).
Lakkum@Jos.19.33.name: Lakkum

Lamech@Gen.4.18-.description: Lamech, a descendant of Cain, was the first polygamist mentioned in the Bible.
Lamech@Gen.4.18-.name: Lamech

Lamech@Gen.5.25-Luk.description: Lamech, the father of Noah, lived 777 years.
Lamech@Gen.5.25-Luk.name: Lamech

Laodicea@Col.2.1-Rev.description: Laodicea, a city in Asia Minor, known for its lukewarm faith (<ref="Revelation 3:14-16">Revelation 3:14-16</ref>).
Laodicea@Col.2.1-Rev.name: Laodicea

Lappidoth@Jdg.4.4.description: Lappidoth, the husband of Deborah, a prophetess and judge in Israel.
Lappidoth@Jdg.4.4.name: Lappidoth

Lasea@Act.27.8.description: Lasea, a city near Fair Havens on the island of Crete (<ref="Act.27.8">Act.27.8</ref>).
Lasea@Act.27.8.name: Lasea

Lasha@Gen.10.19-Num.description: Lasha (Nahaliel), a place marking the extent of Canaanite territory (<ref="Genesis 10:19">Genesis 10:19</ref>) and a stop in Israel's wilderness journey (<ref="Numbers 21:19">Numbers 21:19</ref>).
Lasha@Gen.10.19-Num.name: Lasha

Lasharon@Jos.12.18.description: Lasharon, a Canaanite city whose king was defeated by Joshua (<ref="Joshua 12:18">Joshua 12:18</ref>).
Lasharon@Jos.12.18.name: Lasharon

Lazarus@Jhn.11.1-.description: Lazarus, the brother of Mary and Martha, was raised from the dead by Jesus (<ref="Jhn.11.1-44; 12.1-2,9-11">Jhn.11.1-44; 12.1-2,9-11</ref>).
Lazarus@Jhn.11.1-.name: Lazarus

Lazarus@Luk.16.20-.description: Lazarus, a poor man in Jesus' parable of the rich man and Lazarus (<ref="Luk.16.20-25">Luk.16.20-25</ref>).
Lazarus@Luk.16.20-.name: Lazarus

Leah@Gen.29.16-Rut.description: Leah, the first wife of Jacob and mother of six of his sons and his daughter Dinah.
Leah@Gen.29.16-Rut.name: Leah

Lebanah@Ezr.2.45-Neh.description: Lebanah or Lebana, whose descendants were among the temple servants who returned from the Babylonian exile.
Lebanah@Ezr.2.45-Neh.name: Lebanah

Lebanon@Deu.1.7-Zec.description: Lebanon, a mountainous region north of Israel, known for its cedar trees and as a symbol of strength and beauty (<ref="1Ki.4.33; Psalm 92:12">1Ki.4.33; Psalm 92:12</ref>).
Lebanon@Deu.1.7-Zec.name: Lebanon

Lebanon_Mount@Jdg.3.3.description: Mount Lebanon, a mountain range marking the northern border of the Promised Land (<ref="Judges 3:3">Judges 3:3</ref>).
Lebanon_Mount@Jdg.3.3.name: Lebanon_Mount

Lebanon_Valley@Jos.11.17-.description: The Valley of Lebanon, a valley in the Promised Land conquered by Joshua (<ref="Joshua 11:17; 12:7">Joshua 11:17; 12:7</ref>).
Lebanon_Valley@Jos.11.17-.name: Lebanon_Valley

Lebaoth@Jos.15.32.description: Lebaoth, a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:32">Joshua 15:32</ref>).
Lebaoth@Jos.15.32.name: Lebaoth

Lebonah@Jdg.21.19.description: Lebonah, a place near Shiloh in the territory of Ephraim (<ref="Judges 21:19">Judges 21:19</ref>).
Lebonah@Jdg.21.19.name: Lebonah

Lecah@1Ch.4.21.description: Lecah, a descendant of Judah through Er.
Lecah@1Ch.4.21.name: Lecah

Legion@Mrk.5.9-Luk.description: In the New Testament, Legion is the name given to a demon or group of demons that possessed a man in the region of the Gerasenes (<ref="Mrk.5.9; Luke 8:30">Mrk.5.9; Luke 8:30</ref>).
Legion@Mrk.5.9-Luk.name: Legion

Lehabim@Gen.10.13-1Ch.description: Lehabim, a son of Mizraim and progenitor of a people group.
Lehabim@Gen.10.13-1Ch.name: Lehabim

Lehi@Jdg.15.9-2Sa.description: Lehi, a place where Samson fought against the Philistines and God provided him with water (<ref="Judges 15:9, 14, 19">Judges 15:9, 14, 19</ref>).
Lehi@Jdg.15.9-2Sa.name: Lehi

Lemuel@Pro.31.1-.description: Lemuel, a king whose wise sayings are recorded in Proverbs 31, as taught by his mother.
Lemuel@Pro.31.1-.name: Lemuel

Letushim@Gen.25.3.description: Letushim, a son of Dedan and descendant of Abraham and Keturah.
Letushim@Gen.25.3.name: Letushim

Leummim@Gen.25.3.description: Leummim, a son of Dedan and descendant of Abraham and Keturah.
Leummim@Gen.25.3.name: Leummim

Levi@Gen.29.34-Rev.description: Levi, son of Jacob and Leah, was the progenitor of the Levites, the priestly tribe of Israel.
Levi@Gen.29.34-Rev.name: Levi

Levi@Luk.3.24.description: Levi, son of Melchi, an ancestor of Jesus mentioned in Luke's genealogy (<ref="Luk.3.24">Luk.3.24</ref>).
Levi@Luk.3.24.name: Levi

Levi@Luk.3.29.description: Levi, son of Simeon, an ancestor of Jesus mentioned in Luke's genealogy (<ref="Luk.3.29">Luk.3.29</ref>).
Levi@Luk.3.29.name: Levi

Leviathan@Job.3.8-Isa.description: Leviathan is a large sea creature mentioned in several Old Testament passages, often associated with chaos, evil, or God's power over creation (<ref="Job.3.8; 41:1; Psalm 74:14; 104:26; Isaiah 27:1">Job.3.8; 41:1; Psalm 74:14; 104:26; Isaiah 27:1</ref>).
Leviathan@Job.3.8-Isa.name: Leviathan

Libnah@Jos.10.29-Jer.description: Libnah, a Canaanite city conquered by Joshua (<ref="Joshua 10:29-30">Joshua 10:29-30</ref>) and later designated as a Levitical city (<ref="Joshua 21:13">Joshua 21:13</ref>).
Libnah@Jos.10.29-Jer.name: Libnah

Libnah@Num.33.20-.description: Libnah, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey (<ref="Numbers 33:20-21">Numbers 33:20-21</ref>).
Libnah@Num.33.20-.name: Libnah

Libni@1Ch.6.29.description: Libni, a grandson of Merari and grandson of Levi.
Libni@1Ch.6.29.name: Libni

Libni@Exo.6.17-1Ch.description: Libni or Ladan, a son of Gershon and grandson of Levi.
Libni@Exo.6.17-1Ch.name: Libni

Libya@2Ch.12.3-Act.description: Libya (Put or Pul), a country in North Africa mentioned in various Old Testament prophecies (<ref="Ezk.30.5; 38:5; Nam.3.9">Ezk.30.5; 38:5; Nam.3.9</ref>).
Libya@2Ch.12.3-Act.name: Libya

Likhi@1Ch.7.19.description: Likhi, a son of Shemida and descendant of Manasseh.
Likhi@1Ch.7.19.name: Likhi

Linus@2Ti.4.21.description: Linus, a Christian in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings.
Linus@2Ti.4.21.name: Linus

Lo-ammi@Hos.1.9.description: Lo-ammi, meaning "not my people," was the symbolic name given to Hosea's son, representing God's rejection of Israel.
Lo-ammi@Hos.1.9.name: Lo-ammi

Lo-debar@Jos.13.26-Amo.description: Lo-debar (Debir), a town in Gilead where Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, lived (<ref="2Sa.9.4-5">2Sa.9.4-5</ref>).
Lo-debar@Jos.13.26-Amo.name: Lo-debar

Lo-ruhamah@Hos.1.6-.description: Lo-ruhamah, meaning "not pitied," was the symbolic name given to Hosea's daughter, representing God's withdrawal of mercy from Israel.
Lo-ruhamah@Hos.1.6-.name: Lo-ruhamah

Lod@1Ch.8.12-Act.description: Lod (Lydda), a city in the territory of Benjamin (<ref="1Ch.8.12">1Ch.8.12</ref>), where Peter healed Aeneas <ref="(Act.9.32-35">(Act.9.32-35</ref>).
Lod@1Ch.8.12-Act.name: Lod

Lois@2Ti.1.5.description: Lois, the grandmother of Timothy, was commended by Paul for her sincere faith.
Lois@2Ti.1.5.name: Lois

Lot@Gen.11.27-2Pe.description: Lot, the nephew of Abraham, was rescued from Sodom before its destruction.
Lot@Gen.11.27-2Pe.name: Lot

Lotan@Gen.36.20-1Ch.description: Lotan, a son of Seir the Horite and a chief of Edom.
Lotan@Gen.36.20-1Ch.name: Lotan

Lucifer@Isa.14.12.description: Isaiah poetically describes the king of Babylon as Lucifer, portraying his fall from power.
Lucifer@Isa.14.12.name: Lucifer

Lucius@Act.13.1-Rom.description: Lucius of Cyrene was a prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch who was involved in sending Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary journey.
Lucius@Act.13.1-Rom.name: Lucius

Lud@Gen.10.22-Ezk.description: Lud, a son of Shem and progenitor of the Lydians.
Lud@Gen.10.22-Ezk.name: Lud

Ludim@Gen.10.13-1Ch.description: Ludim, a son of Mizraim and progenitor of a people group.
Ludim@Gen.10.13-1Ch.name: Ludim

Luhith@Isa.15.5-Jer.description: Luhith, a place in Moab mentioned in prophecies of Isaiah and Jeremiah (<ref="Isaiah 15:5; Jeremiah 48:5">Isaiah 15:5; Jeremiah 48:5</ref>).
Luhith@Isa.15.5-Jer.name: Luhith

Luke@2Co.13.13-Phm.description: Luke, a physician and companion of Paul, was the author of the Gospel of Luke and the Book of Acts.
Luke@2Co.13.13-Phm.name: Luke

Luz@Jdg.1.26.description: Luz, a Canaanite city that was destroyed, and another city built by a man who had betrayed the first Luz (<ref="Judges 1:26">Judges 1:26</ref>).
Luz@Jdg.1.26.name: Luz

Lycaonia@Act.14.6-.description: Lycaonia, a region in Asia Minor where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel (<ref="Act.14.6, 11">Act.14.6, 11</ref>).
Lycaonia@Act.14.6-.name: Lycaonia

Lycia@Act.27.5.description: Lycia, a region on the southwest coast of Asia Minor, passed by Paul on his journey to Rome (<ref="Act.27.5">Act.27.5</ref>).
Lycia@Act.27.5.name: Lycia

Lydia@Act.16.14-.description: Lydia, a seller of purple goods from Thyatira, was converted by Paul in Philippi and hosted the church in her home.
Lydia@Act.16.14-.name: Lydia

Lysanias@Luk.3.1.description: Lysanias, the tetrarch of Abilene, ruled during the time of John the Baptist's ministry (<ref="Luk.3.1">Luk.3.1</ref>).
Lysanias@Luk.3.1.name: Lysanias

Lysias@Act.23.26-.description: Claudius Lysias, the Roman commander in Jerusalem, rescued Paul from a Jewish mob and sent him to Felix.
Lysias@Act.23.26-.name: Lysias

Lystra@Act.14.6-2Ti.description: Lystra, a city in Lycaonia where Paul and Barnabas preached and Paul healed a lame man (<ref="Act.14.6-21">Act.14.6-21</ref>).
Lystra@Act.14.6-2Ti.name: Lystra
